title: Someone below me knocked back 🔨
style_prompt: dark blue cinematic night, faceless silhouette, fog, minimal interior, no text, no watermark
hook_text: At 2:42 in the morning I knocked on my floor, and somebody knocked back from underneath.

scenes.narration: At 2:42 in the morning I knocked on my floor, and somebody knocked back from underneath.
I live on the ground floor of a small block. Under my flat is the foundation and a crawl space the size of a coffin, sealed since the day I moved in.
I had been woken by a scratching noise, a patient little scrape, like a spoon on a tin. I rapped on the boards. Three knocks came back, perfectly timed.
I knocked twice. They knocked twice. I knocked four. They knocked four, and a thin voice came up through the floor, saying, finally, you heard me.
I pulled up the rug. The old hatch to the crawl space was there, painted shut. Fresh scratches ran around its edge, dozens of them, from underneath.
The voice said, I have been knocking for eleven years. The woman who lived here before you always turned the telly up. You were the first to listen.
I asked who was down there. It laughed, softly. It said, nobody, anymore, only me, and the hatch, and the hall light that you leave on all night.
Then the paint around the hatch cracked, and the lid lifted by a finger's width, and cold air breathed out of it, smelling of damp earth and my own washing powder.
So tell me. Do you pull the hatch open, or leave it shut?
